llm.summary: This skill is a local document batch-reading helper with no evidence of malicious behavior, though it requests WebSearch despite presenting itself as offline/local.

dimensions.detail: Read/write access is proportionate for reading a corpus and writing summaries, but WebSearch is not explained and is inconsistent with the offline/local positioning.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown metadata, an MIT license, and one Python recovery script; no remote installer, dependency fetching, or execution-on-install behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The multilingual trigger text is broader than ideal, but the actual task framing remains document-study oriented and there is no hidden instruction hijacking or unrelated behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script may run for a bounded polling period and retry failed tasks up to three times, but it does not install services, scheduled tasks, hooks, credential use, or durable agent behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, manifest, and included script align around local batch document reading, DSH inbox/outbox recovery, structured summaries, and retry handling.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent read a local document corpus and write summary files or DSH task files. Consider removing or disabling WebSearch unless you explicitly want external lookups, because the skill otherwise presents itself as local/offline.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted as a real disclosure/scoping note: WebSearch is listed in allowed tools, but the artifact describes offline/local processing and gives no concrete network-use guardrail. No artifact shows actual exfiltration or WebSearch invocation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Partially supported: the language trigger wording is broad, but surrounding content ties the skill to batch document study and does not add unsafe automatic execution.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: the manifest is Chinese, but SKILL.md explicitly declares multilingual input/output support and default same-language replies.
[aig-skill-scan] expected: No A.I.G SARIF security findings were reported, and local inspection did not find remote payload retrieval, persistence, privilege escalation, tool spoofing, or embedded malicious code.
